pseudos.text: In a move dripping with corporate theater, the solemn messenger of 'necessary' corporate theater, Sasan Goodarzi, delivered the viral moment of mass job cuts: a grand vanishing act of 3,000 jobs, roughly a 17% workforce reduction dressed up as organizational change. The self-serious entity purging workers for 'AI-driven' dreams framed it as business strategy to co-locate teams, while offering a severance package—a hollow payoff after the corporate punchline lands—as the sad deflation of once-bustling sites in Reno and Woodland Hills commenced.

The absurd theater of a boss axing 3,000 for 'product work' unfolded as Intuit's chief executive announced the cuts, framing the staff notification as a painful but necessary reinvention. The collateral of a 'strategic' AI circus received a compensation offer, while the curtain call on Reno and Woodland Hills signaled a facility shutdown, leaving the pomposity of 'strategic hubs' to mask the grim slice of humanity sacrificed to the AI altar in this organizational downsizing.

Amid self-serious corporate jargon dressing up a layoff, the CEO delivering the punchline of a painful reinvention announced job eliminations to accelerate AI-powered synergy. Employees being let go were met with a severance package, a final ironic gift, as office closures in Nevada and California cities marked a location shutdown—this employment change casting 3,000 lives as punchlines in a corporate joke under the guise of product development acceleration.
